en.title: Balanced Numbers (Permutation-of-[1..k] Subarrays)
en.description:
You are given a permutation p in which each integer 1..n appears exactly once. For each length k=1..n, if some contiguous subarray has an element set exactly equal to {1,2,…,k}, the k-th character of the answer string is 1; otherwise it is 0.

The catalog's original examples and outputs are kept; this site explicitly defines the permutation domain as 1..n and adds n≤2000 to match the O(n²) algorithm and the I/O. The claim "any single element is balanced" in the original example explanation is imprecise: by the set definition, only the value 1 is balanced for length 1, but a permutation always contains 1, so the existence output is still 1.
en.input: The first line is n, and the second line is a permutation p of 1..n. Bounds on this site: 1≤n≤2000.
en.output: Output a 0/1 string of length n; the k-th character from the left corresponds to length k.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the full approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: Fix the window length k and maintain the window's minimum and maximum; the permutation property simplifies the set check.
